en: Udāna 2.8 Suppavāsāsutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Kuṇḍika in the Kuṇḍadhāna forest.
Now at that time, Suppavāsā the Koliyan daughter had been carrying a fetus for seven years.
For seven days she had been suffering from a difficult labor; afflicted by painful, sharp, harsh, and bitter sensations, she endured them with three thoughts:
“Truly, that Blessed One is a perfectly enlightened Buddha who teaches the Dhamma for the abandoning of such suffering as this!
Truly, the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is well-practiced, practicing for the abandoning of such suffering as this!
Truly, that Nibbāna is most blissful, wherein such suffering as this is not found!”
Then Suppavāsā, the Koliyan daughter, addressed her husband:

“Come, noble son, go to where the Blessed One is; having approached, pay homage with your head at the Blessed One’s feet in my name, and inquire after his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, lightness of body, strength, and well-being, saying:

‘Venerable sir, Suppavāsā, the Koliyan daughter, pays homage with her head at the Blessed One’s feet; she inquires after his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, lightness of body, strength, and well-being.’”
And speak thus:
“Venerable sir, Suppavāsā the Koliyan daughter has carried a fetus for seven years.
For seven days she has been with a difficult labor; afflicted by painful, sharp, harsh, and bitter sensations, she endures it with three thoughts:”
“Truly, that Blessed One is a perfectly enlightened Buddha who teaches the Dhamma for the abandoning of such suffering as this!
Truly, the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is well-practiced, which practices for the abandoning of such suffering as this!
Truly, that Nibbāna is most blissful, wherein such suffering as this is not to be found!”
“Very well,” the Koliyan son replied to Suppavāsā the Koliyan daughter. He then approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side.
As he was sitting there, the Koliyan son said to the Blessed One:

“Venerable sir, Suppavāsā the Koliyan daughter pays homage with her head at the feet of the Blessed One; she inquires after his health, freedom from illness, physical lightness, strength, and well-being.”
And he spoke thus:
"Venerable sir, Suppavāsā, the daughter of the Koliyans, has carried a fetus for seven years.
For seven days she has been suffering from a difficult labor; afflicted by painful, sharp, harsh, and bitter sensations, she endures them with three thoughts:..."
“Truly, that Blessed One is a perfectly enlightened Buddha who teaches the Dhamma for the abandoning of such suffering as this!
Truly, the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is well-practiced, which practices for the abandoning of such suffering as this!
Truly, Nibbāna is most blissful, wherein such suffering as this is not found!”’”
“May Suppavāsā the Koliyan daughter be well; may she give birth to a healthy son, free from illness.
At these words, Suppavāsā the Koliyan daughter gave birth to a healthy son, free from illness, and was herself well.

“So be it, Bhante,” the Koliyan son replied, rejoicing and expressing his appreciation for the Blessed One’s words. He rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, and keeping him to his right, departed for his own home.
The Koliyan youth saw Suppavāsā, the Koliyan daughter, happy and healthy, having given birth to a healthy son.
Upon seeing this, it occurred to him:
"How wonderful, indeed! How marvelous, indeed! Is not the Tathāgata of great psychic power and great majesty?"
"For indeed, as soon as she has spoken with the Blessed One, this Suppavāsā, daughter of the Koliyans,
will give birth to a healthy son, herself being well and free from illness.
He was uplifted, joyful, and filled with rapture and gladness.
Then Suppavāsā, the Koliyan daughter, addressed her husband:
"Come, my lord, go to where the Blessed One is; having approached him, pay homage with your head at the Blessed One’s feet in my name, saying:
‘Venerable sir, Suppavāsā, the Koliyan daughter, pays homage with her head at the Blessed One’s feet.’"
And speak thus:
“Venerable sir, Suppavāsā the Koliyan daughter has carried a fetus for seven years.
Having suffered from a difficult labor for seven days, she is now well and healthy, and has given birth to a healthy son.”
“She invites the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, headed by the Buddha, for a meal for seven days.
‘Venerable sir, may the Blessed One, together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, please accept seven meals from Suppavāsā the Koliyan daughter.

Having agreed to Suppavāsā the Koliyan daughter’s request, saying “Very well,” that Koliyan son approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
Seated to one side, that son of the Koliyans said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, Suppavāsā, the daughter of the Koliyans, pays homage at the feet of the Blessed One with her head and says this:”
“Venerable sir, Suppavāsā the Koliyan daughter carried a fetus for seven years.
For seven days she suffered from a difficult labor, but now she is well and healthy, having given birth to a healthy son.
She invites the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, headed by the Buddha, for a meal for seven days.”
“Venerable sir, may the Blessed One please accept seven meals from Suppavāsā the Koliyan daughter, together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
Now at that time, a certain lay follower had invited the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, headed by the Buddha, for a meal on the following day;
and that lay follower was a supporter of the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna.
Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna:
“Come, Moggallāna, go to where that lay follower is; having approached him, speak thus to that lay follower:
‘Friend, the Koliyan daughter Suppavāsā has carried a fetus for seven years.’”
“Having been in difficult labor for seven days, she is now well and healthy, and has given birth to a healthy son.
She invites the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, headed by the Buddha, for a meal for seven days.
Let Suppavāsā the Koliyan daughter perform these seven meals; you may do yours afterwards.”
“...he is his attendant.
“Very well, Bhante,” the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna replied to the Blessed One. He then went to where that lay follower was, and having approached him, he said to that lay follower:
“Friend, Suppavāsā, the daughter of the Koliyans, has been carrying a pregnancy for seven years.”
“Having been distressed by a difficult labor for seven days, she is now well and healthy, having given birth to a healthy son.
She invites the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, headed by the Buddha, for a meal for seven days.
Let Suppavāsā the Koliyan daughter perform these seven meals; you may do yours afterwards.”
“If, venerable sir, the noble Mahāmoggallāna can guarantee three things for me—
wealth, life, and faith—
then let Suppavāsā the Koliyan daughter prepare seven meals; I shall do it afterwards.”
“Friend, I can stand as guarantor for two things for you:
wealth and life.
But as for faith, you alone must be your own guarantor.”
“If, venerable sir, the noble Mahāmoggallāna is a guarantor for me regarding both my wealth and my life,
let Suppavāsā the Koliyan daughter prepare seven meals; afterwards I shall do so.”
Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, having persuaded that lay follower, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he said this to the Blessed One:
“That lay follower has been persuaded by me, Bhante;
let Suppavāsā, the daughter of the Koliyans, prepare the seven meals first, and he will do so afterwards.”
Then Suppavāsā, the daughter of the Koliyans, for seven days personally served and satisfied the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha with excellent hard and soft foods;
she also had that boy pay homage to the Blessed One and to the entire Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
Then the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the boy:
“I hope it is bearable for you, child; I hope you are getting by; I hope you have no pain?
“From where, Bhante Sāriputta, could there be any bearability for me, from where any getting by?
For seven years I have lived in a copper cauldron of blood.”
Then the Koliyan daughter Suppavāsā, thinking,
“My son is consulting with the General of the Dhamma,” became elated, joyful, and filled with rapture and gladness.
Then the Blessed One, perceiving that the Koliyan daughter Suppavāsā was elated, joyful, and filled with rapture and gladness, said this to her:
“Suppavāsā, would you wish for another son such as this?
“Bhagavā, I would wish for seven more sons such as these.
Then the Blessed One, having understood the significance of this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
The unpleasant in the form of the pleasant,
the unlovely in the form of the lovely,
and suffering in the form of happiness—
“Laxity oversteps its bounds.
Thus ends the eighth [sutta].
